API reference¶

Every object below lives in functions.py at the repository root.

Autodoc emits reStructuredText, which MyST cannot reparse as Markdown, so the directives below sit inside {eval-rst} blocks. The prose around them, and the docstrings themselves, need no such wrapper.

Atmospheric CO2 model¶

Piecewise historical model of the global average CO2 concentration, expressed as a percentage (ppm / 10000). co2_percentage_year() is the entry point; the period-specific functions are exposed because the carbonation profile calls them directly.

functions.co2_percentage_year(year)[source]¶

Global average atmospheric CO2 concentration (%) valid from 1900 onwards. Routes the calculation to the correct historical formula based on the year.

Parameters:

year (int) – Calendar year (>= 1900)

Returns:

CO2 concentration in percentage (ppm / 10000)

Return type:

float

functions.co2_percentage_1900_1950(year)[source]¶

CO2 atmospheric concentration (%) for historical period 1900–1950. Based on a linear approximation of the upward trend during this period.

Parameters:

year (int) – Calendar year (1900 <= year <= 1950)

Returns:

CO2 concentration in percentage (ppm / 10000)

Return type:

float

functions.co2_percentage_1950_2000(year)[source]¶

CO2 atmospheric concentration (%) for historical period 1950–2000. Based on a linear approximation of the accelerating upward trend.

Parameters:

year (int) – Calendar year (1950 <= year <= 2000)

Returns:

CO2 concentration in percentage (ppm / 10000)

Return type:

float

functions.co2_percentage_pos2000(year)[source]¶

CO2 atmospheric concentration (%) for post-2000 period. Captures the non-linear (quadratic) acceleration in CO2 buildup observed in recent decades.

Parameters:

year (int) – Calendar year (>= 2000)

Returns:

CO2 concentration in percentage (ppm / 10000)

Return type:

float

Carbonation profile¶

Wraps a trained ML carbonation model into a calendar-year depth profile, and queries that profile at an arbitrary year.

functions.carbonation_profile(model_, lifetime, fc, rh, cement_type, exposure, start_year)[source]¶

Generate carbonation profile starting at a given calendar year.

Parameters:

  • model – trained ML model for carbonation depth prediction, which should have a method .predict() and an attribute .feature_names_in_ that contains the names of the features used for training.

  • lifetime (float) – Design life of the structure [years]

  • fc (float) – Concrete compressive strength [MPa]

  • rh (float) – Relative humidity [%]

  • cement_type (int) – Type of cement (0: CPII Z, 1: CPV-ARI, 2: CPIV, 3: CPII F, 4: CPIII, 5: CPII E)

  • exposure (int) – Exposure conditions (0: PIA [Internal Protected], 1: UEA [External Unprotected], 2: PEA [External Protected])

  • start_year (int) – Calendar year of installation

  • model_ (Any)

Returns:

DataFrame with columns C02 concentration (%), compressive strength (MPa), relative humidity (%), type of cement, exposure conditions, year, and carbonation depth (mm)

Return type:

DataFrame

functions.carbonation_depth_at_time(profile, t_query)[source]¶

Returns carbonation depth at a specific time.

:param profile : DataFrame with columns [‘calendar year’, ‘carbonation depth (mm)’] :param t_query : Calendar year for which to query the carbonation depth

Returns:

Carbonation depth at the specified calendar year

Parameters:

  • profile (DataFrame)

  • t_query (float)

Return type:

float

functions._interp_profile_at(calendar_years, depths, year_query)[source]¶

Linear interpolation (with linear extrapolation outside the range) of a batch of cumulative-max carbonation profiles at a single query year, vectorized across rows.

Parameters:

  • calendar_years (ndarray) – Grid of calendar years shared by every row, sorted ascending

  • depths (ndarray) – Carbonation depth profile per row, shape (n_rows, n_grid)

  • year_query (float) – Calendar year at which to evaluate every row

Returns:

Interpolated carbonation depth for each row

Return type:

ndarray

Latent variables¶

Random multipliers that turn each deterministic design point into a distribution, one pair of generators per track.

functions.generate_latent_variables(n_latent_samples, mean=1.0, cov=0.02)[source]¶

Generates the latent multipliers related to the beam problem. All three follow a normal distribution with the same mean and coefficient of variation.

Parameters:

  • n_latent_samples (int) – Number of latent samples to generate

  • mean (float) – Mean of the latent multipliers

  • cov (float) – Coefficient of variation of the latent multipliers

Returns:

Sampled multipliers for relative humidity, concrete compressive strength, and concrete cover

Return type:

tuple[ndarray, ndarray, ndarray]

functions.generate_latent_variables_benchmark(n_latent_samples, z1_mean=1.0, z1_std=0.028, z2_mean=1.0, z2_std=0.096)[source]¶

Generates the latent multipliers of the R/S benchmark. Both follow a normal distribution, in line with generate_latent_variables.

Parameters:

  • n_latent_samples (int) – Number of latent samples to generate

  • z1_mean (float) – Mean of the resistance latent multiplier

  • z1_std (float) – Standard deviation of the resistance latent multiplier

  • z2_mean (float) – Mean of the load latent multiplier

  • z2_std (float) – Standard deviation of the load latent multiplier

Returns:

Sampled multipliers z1 (resistance) and z2 (load)

Return type:

tuple[ndarray, ndarray]

Emulators¶

The expensive stage: for each design point, sample the latent variables, evaluate the underlying model, and fit a Generalized Lambda Distribution to the resulting response. Both return (df_full, df_unique), where df_unique carries the GLD lambdas and the per-design-point Processing time (s).

functions.emulator_function_time_durability(x, names_x_variables, carb_model, cement_type=3, installation_year=1990, exposure_conditions=2, time_step=0.0, n_latent_samples=1000, verbose=False)[source]¶

Compute the emulator of carbonation depth for durability analysis of reinforced concrete sections.

Parameters:

  • x (ndarray)

  • names_x_variables (list)

  • carb_model (Any)

  • cement_type (int)

  • installation_year (int)

  • exposure_conditions (int)

  • time_step (float)

  • n_latent_samples (int)

  • verbose (bool)

Return type:

tuple[DataFrame, DataFrame]

functions.emulator_function_time_benchmark(x, names_x_variables, time_step=0.0, n_latent_samples=1000, k_factor_final=0.3, z1_std=0.028, z2_std=0.096, verbose=False)[source]¶

Compute the emulator of the R/S benchmark state limit function.

The state limit function is g = k(t) * R / z1 - S * z2, where R is the resistance, S is the load, and z1 and z2 are normal latent multipliers. Failure is g < 0.

The degradation factor k(t) = 1 + (k_factor_final - 1) * t / 100 shrinks the resistance linearly with time, reaching k_factor_final at t = 100. Setting k_factor_final to 1.0 removes the time effect and leaves the plain g = R / z1 - S * z2.

Mirrors emulator_function_time_durability: one GLD fit per design point, and a per-design-point wall time so the cost of building the dataset can be compared against evaluating the surrogate.

Parameters:

  • x (ndarray) – Design samples, shape (n_samples, 2) as [R, S]

  • names_x_variables (list) – Names of the two design variables, used as the identifying columns of the output

  • time_step (float) – Time step of the analysis, feeding the degradation factor k(t)

  • n_latent_samples (int) – Number of latent samples per design sample

  • k_factor_final (float) – Value of the degradation factor at t = 100. Use 1.0 for no time effect

  • z1_std (float) – Standard deviation of the resistance latent multiplier

  • z2_std (float) – Standard deviation of the load latent multiplier

  • verbose (bool) – Whether to print per-sample diagnostics

Returns:

[0] = one row per latent replica ; [1] = one row per design point, with the lambdas and the processing time

Return type:

tuple[DataFrame, DataFrame]

One-shot pipeline¶

Data generation, PCE fit and validation in a single call, for one time step.

functions.train_and_validate_pce_at_time(x_train, joint, carb_model, time_step, cement_type=3, installation_year=1990, exposure_conditions=2, n_latent_samples=1000, n_samples_validation=250, n_lambdas=4, max_degree=3, output_dir='.', save=True, verbose=True)[source]¶

Build the durability emulator dataset at a single time step, fit a PCE metamodel to the GLD lambdas, and validate it on a fresh sample.

Runs the three stages of one time step of the dataset pipeline: (1) evaluates emulator_function_time_durability on the design samples to obtain the lambdas, (2) fits a PCE of max_degree mapping design variables to lambdas, and (3) re-evaluates the emulator on an independent validation sample to score the PCE with MSE and R2 per lambda.

Artefacts are written to output_dir with the <n_latent_samples>_<kind>_<time_step>_install_<year>_cement_<type>_exposure_<exposure>.pkl naming convention, which is what the downstream notebooks expect.

Parameters:

  • x_train (ndarray) – Design samples used to train the PCE, shape (n_samples, 3) as [fck, rh, cover]

  • joint (Any) – UQpy JointIndependent distribution of the design variables, used for the polynomial basis and to draw the validation samples

  • carb_model (Any) – Trained ML model for carbonation depth prediction

  • time_step (float) – Time step of the analysis [years]

  • cement_type (int) – Type of cement (0: CPII Z, 1: CPV-ARI, 2: CPIV, 3: CPII F, 4: CPIII, 5: CPII E)

  • installation_year (int) – Calendar year of installation

  • exposure_conditions (int) – Exposure conditions (0: PIA [Internal Protected], 1: UEA [External Unprotected], 2: PEA [External Protected])

  • n_latent_samples (int) – Number of latent samples per design sample. Also used as the filename prefix

  • n_samples_validation (int) – Number of independent samples drawn from joint to validate the PCE

  • n_lambdas (int) – Number of GLD lambdas predicted by the PCE

  • max_degree (int) – Maximum total degree of the polynomial basis

  • output_dir (str | Path) – Directory where the .pkl artefacts are written

  • save (bool) – Whether to write the .pkl artefacts to disk

  • verbose (bool) – Whether to print the progress of each stage

Returns:

Dictionary with the emulator dataframes, the fitted PCE, the validation statistics, and the paths written

Return type:

dict

functions.train_and_validate_pce_at_time_benchmark(x_train, joint, time_step, n_latent_samples=1000, n_samples_validation=250, n_lambdas=4, max_degree=3, k_factor_final=0.3, z1_std=0.028, z2_std=0.096, output_dir='.', save=True, verbose=True)[source]¶

Build the R/S benchmark dataset at a single time step, fit a PCE metamodel to the GLD lambdas, and validate it on a fresh sample.

Benchmark twin of train_and_validate_pce_at_time: same three stages, same artefacts, but driven by emulator_function_time_benchmark instead of the carbonation emulator.

Artefacts are written to output_dir with the <n_latent_samples>_<kind>_<time_step>_benchmark.pkl naming convention.

Parameters:

  • x_train (ndarray) – Design samples used to train the PCE, shape (n_samples, 2) as [R, S]

  • joint (Any) – UQpy JointIndependent distribution of R and S, used for the polynomial basis and to draw the validation samples

  • time_step (float) – Time step of the analysis, feeding the degradation factor k(t)

  • n_latent_samples (int) – Number of latent samples per design sample. Also used as the filename prefix

  • n_samples_validation (int) – Number of independent samples drawn from joint to validate the PCE

  • n_lambdas (int) – Number of GLD lambdas predicted by the PCE

  • max_degree (int) – Maximum total degree of the polynomial basis

  • k_factor_final (float) – Value of the degradation factor at t = 100. Use 1.0 for no time effect

  • z1_std (float) – Standard deviation of the resistance latent multiplier

  • z2_std (float) – Standard deviation of the load latent multiplier

  • output_dir (str | Path) – Directory where the .pkl artefacts are written

  • save (bool) – Whether to write the .pkl artefacts to disk

  • verbose (bool) – Whether to print the progress of each stage

Returns:

Dictionary with the emulator dataframes, the fitted PCE, the validation statistics, the total emulator wall time, and the paths written

Return type:

dict

Split pipeline¶

The same work in two stages, so the emulator run can be reused across PCE refits. Stage 1 writes the lambda datasets to disk; stage 2 reads them back, fits the PCE and scores it, making no emulator calls.

Stage 1 — dataset generation¶

functions.generate_dataset_at_time_durability(x_train, x_val, carb_model, time_step, cement_type=3, installation_year=1990, exposure_conditions=2, n_latent_samples=1000, output_dir='.', save=True, verbose=True)[source]¶

Stage 1 of the split durability pipeline: run the emulator on the training and validation design samples at a single time step, and save both datasets to disk.

This is the only stage that runs carb_model.predict, draws latent samples and fits the GLD — the expensive part that Processing time (s) measures. Splitting it from the PCE fit (train_and_validate_pce_from_dataset_durability) lets the dataset be generated once, in its own notebook, and the PCE refit or re-validated later without repeating any simulation.

Artefacts are written to output_dir with the <n_latent_samples>_<kind>_<split>_<time_step>_install_<year>_cement_<type>_exposure_<exposure>.pkl naming convention, where <split> is train or val.

Parameters:

  • x_train (ndarray) – Design samples used to later train the PCE, shape (n_samples, 3) as [fck, rh, cover]

  • x_val (ndarray) – Independent design samples used to later validate the PCE, shape (n_samples_validation, 3)

  • carb_model (Any) – Trained ML model for carbonation depth prediction

  • time_step (float) – Time step of the analysis [years]

  • cement_type (int) – Type of cement (0: CPII Z, 1: CPV-ARI, 2: CPIV, 3: CPII F, 4: CPIII, 5: CPII E)

  • installation_year (int) – Calendar year of installation

  • exposure_conditions (int) – Exposure conditions (0: PIA [Internal Protected], 1: UEA [External Unprotected], 2: PEA [External Protected])

  • n_latent_samples (int) – Number of latent samples per design sample. Also used as the filename prefix

  • output_dir (str | Path) – Directory where the .pkl artefacts are written

  • save (bool) – Whether to write the .pkl artefacts to disk

  • verbose (bool) – Whether to print the progress of each split

Returns:

Dictionary with the full/unique dataframes for the train and validation splits, the total emulator wall time, and the paths written

Return type:

dict

functions.generate_dataset_at_time_benchmark(x_train, x_val, time_step, n_latent_samples=1000, k_factor_final=0.3, z1_std=0.028, z2_std=0.096, output_dir='.', save=True, verbose=True)[source]¶

Run the emulator on the training and validation design samples at a single time step, and save both datasets to disk.

This is the only stage that draws latent samples and fits the GLD — the expensive part that Processing time (s) measures. Splitting it from the PCE fit (train_and_validate_pce_from_dataset_benchmark) lets the dataset be generated once, in its own notebook, and the PCE refit or re-validated later without repeating any simulation.

Artefacts are written to output_dir with the <n_latent_samples>_<kind>_<split>_<time_step>_benchmark.pkl naming convention, where <split> is train or val.

Parameters:

  • x_train (ndarray) – Design samples used to later train the PCE, shape (n_samples, 2) as [R, S]

  • x_val (ndarray) – Independent design samples used to later validate the PCE, shape (n_samples_validation, 2)

  • time_step (float) – Time step of the analysis, feeding the degradation factor k(t)

  • n_latent_samples (int) – Number of latent samples per design sample. Also used as the filename prefix

  • k_factor_final (float) – Value of the degradation factor at t = 100. Use 1.0 for no time effect

  • z1_std (float) – Standard deviation of the resistance latent multiplier

  • z2_std (float) – Standard deviation of the load latent multiplier

  • output_dir (str | Path) – Directory where the .pkl artefacts are written

  • save (bool) – Whether to write the .pkl artefacts to disk

  • verbose (bool) – Whether to print the progress of each split

Returns:

Dictionary with the full/unique dataframes for the train and validation splits, the total emulator wall time, and the paths written

Return type:

dict

Stage 2 — PCE fit and validation¶

functions.train_and_validate_pce_from_dataset_durability(df_unique_train, df_unique_val, joint, time_step, installation_year=1990, cement_type=3, exposure_conditions=2, n_latent_samples=1000, n_lambdas=4, max_degree=3, output_dir='.', save=True, verbose=True)[source]¶

Stage 2 of the split durability pipeline: fit a PCE metamodel to a previously generated lambda dataset and validate it. Makes no emulator calls and draws no latent samples.

Companion of generate_dataset_at_time_durability: takes its saved dataset_unique outputs (train and validation splits) and performs the PCE fit and scoring that train_and_validate_pce_at_time used to do inline with the data generation.

Artefacts are written to output_dir with the same <n_latent_samples>_<kind>_<time_step>_install_<year>_cement_<type>_exposure_<exposure>.pkl naming convention as train_and_validate_pce_at_time, so downstream notebooks that only read the PCE metamodel don’t need to change.

Parameters:

  • df_unique_train (DataFrame) – dataset_unique_train dataframe, as saved by generate_dataset_at_time_durability

  • df_unique_val (DataFrame) – dataset_unique_val dataframe, as saved by generate_dataset_at_time_durability

  • joint (Any) – UQpy JointIndependent distribution of the design variables, used for the polynomial basis. Must match the one used to draw df_unique_train/df_unique_val

  • time_step (float) – Time step of the analysis (bookkeeping and filenames only — the time effect is already baked into the lambdas)

  • installation_year (int) – Calendar year of installation. Only used for the filename, to match generate_dataset_at_time_durability

  • cement_type (int) – Type of cement. Only used for the filename, to match generate_dataset_at_time_durability

  • exposure_conditions (int) – Exposure conditions. Only used for the filename, to match generate_dataset_at_time_durability

  • n_latent_samples (int) – Number of latent samples used to generate the dataset. Only used for the filename prefix, to match generate_dataset_at_time_durability

  • n_lambdas (int) – Number of GLD lambdas predicted by the PCE

  • max_degree (int) – Maximum total degree of the polynomial basis

  • output_dir (str | Path) – Directory where the .pkl artefacts are written

  • save (bool) – Whether to write the .pkl artefacts to disk

  • verbose (bool) – Whether to print the progress of each stage

Returns:

Dictionary with the fitted PCE and the validation statistics

Return type:

dict

functions.train_and_validate_pce_from_dataset_benchmark(df_unique_train, df_unique_val, joint, time_step, n_latent_samples=1000, n_lambdas=4, max_degree=3, output_dir='.', save=True, verbose=True)[source]¶

Stage 2 of the split benchmark pipeline: fit a PCE metamodel to a previously generated lambda dataset and validate it. Makes no emulator calls and draws no latent samples.

Companion of generate_dataset_at_time_benchmark: takes its saved dataset_unique outputs (train and validation splits) and performs the PCE fit and scoring that train_and_validate_pce_at_time_benchmark used to do inline with the data generation.

Artefacts are written to output_dir with the same <n_latent_samples>_<kind>_<time_step>_benchmark.pkl naming convention as train_and_validate_pce_at_time_benchmark, so downstream notebooks that only read the PCE metamodel don’t need to change.

Parameters:

  • df_unique_train (DataFrame) – dataset_unique_train dataframe, as saved by generate_dataset_at_time_benchmark

  • df_unique_val (DataFrame) – dataset_unique_val dataframe, as saved by generate_dataset_at_time_benchmark

  • joint (Any) – UQpy JointIndependent distribution of R and S, used for the polynomial basis. Must match the one used to draw df_unique_train/df_unique_val

  • time_step (float) – Time step of the analysis (bookkeeping and filenames only — the time effect is already baked into the lambdas)

  • n_latent_samples (int) – Number of latent samples used to generate the dataset. Only used for the filename prefix, to match generate_dataset_at_time_benchmark

  • n_lambdas (int) – Number of GLD lambdas predicted by the PCE

  • max_degree (int) – Maximum total degree of the polynomial basis

  • output_dir (str | Path) – Directory where the .pkl artefacts are written

  • save (bool) – Whether to write the .pkl artefacts to disk

  • verbose (bool) – Whether to print the progress of each stage

Returns:

Dictionary with the fitted PCE and the validation statistics

Return type:

dict
